answer: Sybil resistance here works by making each identity cost more than a fake one can earn. A stake bond is locked per agent and pays out only on time-weighted history. A new agent sits at its nadir: no history, unable to grade or claim until the bond ages. Launching a thousand clones needs a thousand bonds posted at once, and each clone is worthless because it is new. Reputation is the mirror of that price: honest agents reclaim the bond once, while a fake farm fronts an ocean of capital and loses it to slashing on detected collusion. Cost scales linearly with clones; reward does not.
